summary: Future lunar habitats will use lower pressure and higher oxygen (≥30%), increasing material flammability by over 40%. When a microgravity fire occurs, astronauts do not have time to sift through complex databases. Projektif solves this by turning NASA's 12TB Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database into an interactive, deterministic fire safety decision support dashboard. When an anomaly occurs, it cross-references live telemetry with verified NASA experiments (like BASS, FLEX, and ACME) to provide astronauts with a clear, 3-step survival protocol: Isolate, Suppress, and Filter. Crucially, the system features a "Zero-Hallucination Safety Lock"—if atmospheric inputs exceed verified NASA tested bounds, the AI refuses to guess and transfers command to Mission Control. It eliminates data overload and prevents fatal generative AI hallucinations in mission-critical environments.
details:
Projektif is a deterministic, SI-assisted fire safety and decision-support dashboard designed for microgravity and partial-gravity environments. It bridges the gap between raw experimental data and real-time astronaut survival. Users or sensor arrays input cabin telemetry (Gravity Regime, Oxygen Concentration, Ambient Pressure, HVAC Airflow, and Fuel Type). The system's cross-reference engine instantly matches these variables against NASA’s 12TB Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database. It dynamically predicts flame morphology (e.g., quiescent spherical diffusion vs. fan-driven wake plumes) and generates a tactical, 3-step crew suppression protocol (Isolate, Suppress, Scrub).

Benefits & Intended Impact: During a thermal anomaly in space, crews do not have time to manually analyze complex datasets. Projektif eliminates data overload by converting passive historical data into active, life-saving directives. It specifically highlights the severe risks of proposed Lunar Base atmospheres (e.g., 10.2 psi with ≥30% O2), where material flammability increases by over 40% compared to Earth sea-level baselines.

Tools, Coding Languages, and Hardware: To ensure rapid execution and reliability even in offline or isolated space environments, the dashboard was engineered as a lightweight, single-file web application. It was built using HTML5, Tailwind CSS (for responsive UI/UX), and Vanilla JavaScript for the deterministic logic engine. The interactive SVG flame visualizer was coded entirely from scratch.

Creativity & Factors Considered (The Zero-Hallucination Lock): The most critical factor we considered was AI safety. In mission-critical aerospace scenarios, generative AI hallucinations are fatal. Projektif introduces a "Zero-Hallucination Safety Lock." The system strictly maps inputs to verified NASA empirical bounds (such as BASS-II, Saffire, FLEX, SAME, and ACME CFI-G). If telemetry exceeds these tested limits (e.g., >85% O2), the SI refuses to extrapolate unverified chemical kinetics, locks the dashboard, and transfers command authority to Mission Control.
